examples.solution_text:
First find the base diagonal in $\triangle ABC$.
$\begin{align*}AC^2&=9^2+12^2\\AC^2&=225\\AC&=15\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
a. The angle with the base is $\theta=\angle TAC$. In $\triangle ACT$, the height is opposite $\theta$ and the base diagonal is adjacent.
$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{6}{15}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{6}{15}\right)\\\theta&\approx21.8^\circ\end{align*}$
b. The angle with the vertical edge is $\phi=\angle ATC$. The base diagonal is now opposite the required angle.
$\begin{align*}\tan\phi&=\frac{15}{6}\\\phi&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{15}{6}\right)\\\phi&\approx68.2^\circ\end{align*}$

a. The face angle is $\angle TMC$. The section is perpendicular to the base edge, so $CM$ is half the base side.
$\begin{align*}CM&=\frac{10}{2}\\CM&=5\text{ cm}\\\tan\angle TMC&=\frac{5}{5}\\\angle TMC&=45.0^\circ\end{align*}$
b. The slant-edge angle is $\angle TQC$. Its horizontal leg $CQ$ is half the base diagonal.
$\begin{align*}\text{Base diagonal}&=\sqrt{10^2+10^2}\\&=10\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\\CQ&=\frac{10\sqrt{2}}{2}\\CQ&=5\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
Keep the diagonal exact when calculating the angle.
$\begin{align*}\tan\angle TQC&=\frac{5}{5\sqrt{2}}\\\angle TQC&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{5\sqrt{2}}\right)\\\angle TQC&\approx35.3^\circ\end{align*}$

The plane angle is $\angle HAD$, measured in the section perpendicular to the common edge. Use the depth and height in $\triangle ADH$.
$\begin{align*}\tan\angle HAD&=\frac{DH}{AD}\\\tan\angle HAD&=\frac{6}{6}\\\angle HAD&=45^\circ\end{align*}$

Each angle of depression equals the corresponding angle of elevation, so both elevation triangles have a $45^\circ$ angle at sea level.
$\begin{align*}OA&=\frac{50}{\tan45^\circ}\\OA&=50\text{ m}\\OB&=\frac{50}{\tan45^\circ}\\OB&=50\text{ m}\end{align*}$
Reverse the bearings to draw the directions from $O$.
$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of }A\text{ from }O&=60^\circ+180^\circ=240^\circ\\\text{Bearing of }B\text{ from }O&=150^\circ+180^\circ=330^\circ\\\angle AOB&=330^\circ-240^\circ=90^\circ\end{align*}$
Use Pythagoras in the ground triangle.
$\begin{align*}AB&=\sqrt{50^2+50^2}\\AB&=50\sqrt{2}\text{ m}\\AB&\approx71\text{ m}\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: AC=sqrt(9²+12²)=15 cm. The base angle is atan(6/15)=21.8014…°, giving 21.8°. The vertical-edge angle is atan(15/6)=68.1986…°, giving 68.2°. The two angles sum to 90°.
CM=10/2=5 cm, so the face angle is atan(5/5)=45.0°. The base diagonal is 10sqrt(2) cm and CQ=5sqrt(2) cm. The slant-edge angle is atan(5/(5sqrt(2)))=35.2644…°, giving 35.3°.
In the section perpendicular to the common front edge, AD=6 cm and DH=6 cm. The plane angle is angle HAD=atan(6/6)=45°. The prism length is unnecessary for this section.
AC=60/tan45°=60 m and BC=60/tan30°=60sqrt(3) m. The ground directions are perpendicular, so AB=sqrt(60²+(60sqrt(3))²)=120 m.
Depression equals elevation, giving OA=OB=50/tan45°=50 m. The reverse bearings are 240°T and 330°T, separated by 90°. AB=sqrt(50²+50²)=50sqrt(2)=70.7107… m, rounding to 71 m.
The ground triangle is right-angled at C, with angle CPQ=30°. CQ=100sin30°=50 m. In triangle QCT, h=CQ tan45°=50 m.
PC=100cos30°=50sqrt(3) m and CQ=100sin30°=50 m. The elevation from P gives h=50sqrt(3)tan30°=50 m. Therefore the elevation from Q is atan(h/CQ)=atan(1)=45°.
